minutes.headline: Building committee agreed to price EV chargers, basement slab and solar as bid alternates; two chargers likely; no votes.
minutes.summary: The committee discussed what dollar amount to request at annual town meeting for the municipal building project, working from a lower and a higher estimate that differ by soft-cost markups. Members leaned toward including only about two EV chargers in the base project, leaving the meeting house basement slab out, and pricing add-ons as bid alternates. They also covered solar canopy concerns from an abutter, unsurveyed hazardous materials, and public-engagement feedback from social media. No formal votes were taken.

public_comment.topic: Asked how the solar panel canopy fits the architectural preservation district; raised abutter view and screening concerns, and whether the parking lot affects the School Street right of way.

budget_items.what_was_said: Bond counsel is calculating 20-year or 30-year repayment estimates, expected by end of month and going to the town manager. Debt that falls off will be considered in the homeowner impact.
The high estimate was temporarily plugged in for presentation purposes while the actual request is decided.
The architect's email explained the step from the independently estimated construction cost to the low and high total project estimates via soft-cost markups.
The estimate excludes the photovoltaic canopy, code-required EV charger equipment and the meeting house basement slab; remediation was also said not to be included.
Members said only the code-required infrastructure is needed and favored about two chargers, with the rest priced as an alternate.
The slab was estimated at a high per-square-foot price; members favored keeping it as a priced alternate rather than in the request.
Inflation Reduction Act funding was described as frozen, which would leave the town responsible for more of the canopy cost.
The chair will work with bond counsel on escalators for the phased construction; the higher estimate is currently being used.
A more detailed breakdown of owner's project manager, design and contingency costs is needed. The OPM fee was described as a standard percentage.

what_happened.line: The committee took no votes, but agreed generally to price about two EV chargers, with the supporting infrastructure, as part of the project.
Members agreed the meeting house basement slab stays a bid alternate rather than part of the base request.
The EV chargers, slab and solar are to be put out in the bid for pricing as alternates, even if town meeting does not authorize them.
The chair will continue with bond counsel on cost escalators, using the higher estimate for now, and will ask the project engineer about hazardous materials.
Members said a detailed breakdown of soft costs and contingency is needed for the public.

why_it_matters: The amount requested at annual town meeting and the borrowing behind it set the debt a homeowner's tax bill would carry, and the figure still depends on which estimate is used and which items are left out.
Items priced as alternates sit outside the base request, so the town could learn their cost at bid without having been asked to authorize them.

The detailed soft-cost and contingency breakdown, and the final request amount for the annual town meeting warrant article.
